charts.title: Estimated Annual Endowment Tax Bills Under OBBBA (8% Bracket)
charts.footnote: AEI projections based on IRS Form 990 filings and IPEDS enrollment data. Princeton may avoid top bracket via financial aid restructuring. Brown is below the $500K-per-student threshold and pays no new tax.

charts.title: Class of 2030 Ivy League Acceptance Rates (Published Data)
charts.sourceUrl: Note: Source attribution includes Oriel Admissions (consultancy)
charts.linkText: Read full Forbes Ivy Day coverage
charts.footnote: Harvard, Princeton, Penn, Cornell, and Dartmouth withheld official acceptance rate data for the second consecutive year. Figures for those schools are estimates from institutional reporting and data trackers. Brown and Yale figures are from official institutional releases.

charts.title: Federal Funding Frozen / Settled: Selected Ivy and Peer Institutions
charts.footnote: Figures reflect the amount of federal funding frozen or withheld at peak, not final settlement amounts. Brown's settlement was $50M in RI workforce grants (no Treasury payment); Cornell's was $30M in agricultural research. Harvard has not settled; freeze amount reflects court-restored funding subject to ongoing appeal.

charts.title: U.S. International Student Enrollment Decline: Spring 2026 vs. Spring 2025
charts.linkText: Read full TIME / NAFSA international enrollment report
charts.footnote: Survey of 149 U.S. institutions. Overall figure reflects spring 2026 vs. spring 2025. Graduate decline is average across all responding institutions. Share reporting lower enrollment is percent of the 149 surveyed schools.
